correct_answer: Appeal the 12 claims from Active-VHP providers under the master agreement immediately, and escalate credentialing for the remaining 22 providers with resubmission before the 60-day timely filing window closes on the earliest DOS (April 30, 2026)
rationale: This requires synthesizing information across five systems to understand the full picture. The 12 providers already showing Active-VHP status in Epic's credentialing module are covered under the VHP master agreement -- their denials are straightforward appeals with strong contractual basis. The remaining 22 are in Pending-Transition status because HealthFirst never completed processing the roster (the only confirmation was a verbal phone call mentioned in Teams, with no written follow-up). The critical deadline is the timely filing limit: HealthFirst has a 60-day window from DOS per the guidelines document. The earliest March DOS (03/01) means the absolute deadline is April 30, 2026 -- not 60 days from denial date. Option A incorrectly assumes the master agreement already covers Riverside (it does not until credentialing completes). Option B correctly identifies the credentialing gap but miscalculates the deadline -- timely filing runs from DOS, not from denial date, making the earliest deadline April 30, not May 30. Option D tries to resurrect an expired contract whose transition period explicitly ended 12/31/2025.
